pitchei-teshuva/part-001.txt|1|_: As a paid custodian (shomer sachar). Avkat Taharat HaKodesh cites this in the name of Mordekhai, and Rama already brought this law in Choshen Mishpat siman 120 and siman 176.
pitchei-teshuva/part-001.txt|2|_: Since from the outset. Avkat Taharat HaKodesh s.k. 18 in the name of Taz — from this one may learn, etc. And see Levushei Serad, who wrote that some say the recipient is not obligated to give him unless he wishes to give; there is no ribbis prohibition in that case, and therefore it is a safek in the law and we do not extract from the borrower; and if the lender seized payment we do not remove it from him. Scribes should be instructed to specify in the iska document, with the borrower's knowledge, that even after the repayment date he remains obligated to pay him.
pitchei-teshuva/part-001.txt|3|_: One may be lenient in this. So too is the view of Radbaz in Teshuvot HaChadashot end of siman 497 — see there.
pitchei-teshuva/part-001.txt|4|_: This is full-fledged ribbis. See responsum of R' Eliyahu Mizrachi siman 23, who wrote that nevertheless it is obvious there is no issue of ribbis ketzutza here, and therefore it is permitted to lend orphans' money in such a manner — see there.
pitchei-teshuva/part-001.txt|5|_: He deposited money. Avkat Taharat HaKodesh — and see Dagul MeRevavah, who wrote that this is when they so stipulated verbally; but if they performed kinyan with him or made an iska document, he is obligated even after the loan — see there.
pitchei-teshuva/part-001.txt|6|_: And he writes them as a loan. Avkat Taharat HaKodesh — and see Dagul MeRevavah, who wrote that Bach's words here contradict his words in CM; he concludes therefore in my humble opinion that even if Rosh wrote it is forbidden to take profit as Bach copied there, that applies only to the beginning of Rosh's words where ribbis was combined with principal; but where only principal was written and the iska was stipulated verbally, it is forbidden only to do so initially, but if he transgressed and did so, it is permitted to accept if the borrower gives willingly, and the borrower is even obligated to give half the profit per the condition — see there. I once met my friend R' Shmuel, dayan of our community, who showed me his writings challenging Dagul MeRevavah, for in Rosh klal 88 din 7 it is explicit that even if only principal was written and the iska was verbal, it is forbidden to benefit and take any ribbis; Rosh did not mention combining ribbis with principal at all — see there [and see Chavat Shalom siman 27].
pitchei-teshuva/part-001.txt|8|_: By themselves. Avkat Taharat HaKodesh — and where there is safek in the law [see Chatam Sofer siman 241] — and see responsum Brit Avraham vol. 14 siman 49 letter 1 in Hagahah, who ruled that if the safek is whether it is ribbis ketzutza or avak ribbis, it is a safek issur lechumra and he must return it since it came to his hand improperly; but in safek whether ribbis ketzutza or entirely permitted, he may say kimsli — see there — and he concludes the halachah follows the arbitrator.
rabbi-akiva-eiger-yd/part-001.txt|1|_: (Siman 177 seif 5 in Hagahah) Misusing the deposit in this way. In my humble opinion Rashba in the responsum Beit Yosef brought (CM 176, new 36) and so too in Rashba's chiddushim on Bava Kamma disagrees, that even if he misused part of the business and engaged in the rest without specification and profited, the profit is split — see there; and it requires study.
mechaber/part-001.txt|25|main: If it is written in the document "half in profit and half in loss," and the giver or recipient is a prominent person known not to violate ribbis, we rule leniently and say: if he takes half the profit, he must accept two-thirds of the responsibility; and if he accepts only half the responsibility, he takes only a third of the profit. But with an ordinary person not presumed so, we judge the document literally and it is a document containing ribbis — if there is loss he loses half per his stipulation, and if there is profit he receives nothing. {Rama: And likewise any iska done in violation (responsum Rosh klal 88).}
beer-hagolah/part-001.txt|1|_: Rambam's language in chapter 8 of Hilchot Malveh veLoveh law 12, from Mishnah Bava Metzia 70b, per Rashi's explanation there:
beer-hagolah/part-001.txt|4|_: Rambam's language in chapter 6 of Hilchot Sheluchin veShutfim law 2, from the baraita there as Abbaye explains: (°) Rashi explains — if he was a smith or carpenter, how much would a person take to idle from heavy labor and do light work; and so implied from Rif and Tosafot — idle worker means completely idle with no work at all, how much he would take to engage in this business; and so Rosh there. He further wrote that here the Sages were lenient regarding avak ribbis, and for a small amount given it does not appear as ribbis; and so Tur:
beer-hagolah/part-001.txt|9|_: Rambam's language there law 3, from the incident of the sons of Rav Ilish there 68b, per his explanation:
beer-hagolah/part-001.txt|18|_: Same there — he wrote we do not say that since according to the claimant he is wicked he is not believed with an oath: (°) And so CM siman 82 seif 10; and in my humble opinion this does not disagree with what was written above siman 169, for there he claims he took it permissibly and mentions the heter via a gentile, and is believed per prozbul law, unlike here in siman 82 where he denies everything and does not claim permissibility, so we impose an oath; and I have not found the book Rama cites as disagreeing — end quote.
beer-hagolah/part-001.txt|19|_: Semag negative precepts siman 193 in the name of Rabbeinu Yaakov, because a person does not make himself wicked:
beer-hagolah/part-001.txt|20|_: Mordekhai in chapter 5 of Bava Metzia in the name of responsum Maharam: (°) Meaning even though it appears as an evasion and surely the borrower will not withhold the lender's money, nevertheless it is permitted:
beer-hagolah/part-001.txt|35|_: There 68a — the halachah is not like the documents of Mechoza, etc.:
beer-hagolah/part-001.txt|37|_: The incident of the sons of Rav Ilish, as Rava said, etc., there 68b, per Rashi and Tosafot there:
baer-heitev/part-001.txt|4|_: A third. Shach wrote this is Rambam's view, but most poskim disagree and hold the recipient takes two-thirds of profit and bears half the loss — and so is the main view in Shas; however all this is in unspecified cases, but where there is a known custom we follow custom where there is no prohibition. Taz wrote that if the recipient already gave the giver principal and profit (and did not claim wages at all), he has no claim against him for this is asmakhta and courts do not extract; but if he has not yet given back his principal he may withhold from the principal for his wages; however if he already gave principal and profit and did not claim wages, and afterward claimed wages while the recipient owes him another debt and wished to deduct wages — it appears he cannot deduct since at time of paying principal he asked for nothing and it is complete mechilah (see Perach Mateh Aharon siman 21 and 116):
baer-heitev/part-001.txt|5|ב: Yeshnah — specifically here where it is rabbinically permitted in such a case, but not for biblical ribbis. Shach:
baer-heitev/part-001.txt|6|ג: Ketzutza — meaning there is no iska there, only a loan; Shach wrote this law is uncertain, for it seems from all poskim even biblical ribbis is permitted when the recipient accepts all responsibility — see what he expands there:
baer-heitev/part-001.txt|7|ב: Alah. Mordekhai wrote we give the recipient [credit] for his reliability — if it seems to him that it rose so much we do not impose an oath on doubt but tell him, remember we rely on your reliability; Bach wrote the reason is simple we do not impose an oath because he does not claim certainly; Shach wrote even if he claims certainly the lender is exempt without oath if he says I took it permissibly as above siman 169 s.k. 35; Taz wrote from this we learn regarding one who does iska permissibly until a set time, and after that time the money remains in his hand as before without renewing the heter — the recipient cannot say I will not give you profit after that time, since initially the money came to him permissibly it certainly continues after the time; and this is a fortiori from the law mentioned here that he explicitly made it a loan:
baer-heitev/part-001.txt|12|_: He is not [believed]. Shach wrote that although if he wished he could exempt himself at repayment etc. he is not believed, for a person does not make himself wicked — and it implies even for a verbal loan he is not believed:
baer-heitev/part-001.txt|17|_: Who forbids. Bach wrote in the name of Acharonim that specifically at time of loan it is forbidden to do so initially, but if he already lent him on collateral and now says if you do not repay me the collateral is yours from now — permitted; Shach wrote it requires study, for there are those who permit above seif 14 implying they disagree since he does not give him money at the end; perhaps one can distinguish between collateral initially in his possession which is worse:
baer-heitev/part-001.txt|18|א: And they acquired from him. Regarding that it is not asmakhta as in CM siman 207 — here all agree it is permitted since it is a penalty method, but forbidden due to ribbis evasion; here in selling merchandise to him since it is a penalty method even ribbis evasion does not apply — Shach; Bach wrote specifically when he stipulated to give for it immediately at that time a hundred gold coins, but if the condition was that if he does not give merchandise in half a year he will give a hundred gold coins after the year ends, it is full ribbis; Shach wrote he is not compelled except when he stipulated explicitly that if he does not give in half a year he will give a hundred gold coins when the year ends and the lender must wait until the year ends — in that case it appears to be full ribbis, and none require six [months], and Taz's view leans similarly — see there:
baer-heitev/part-001.txt|23|_: Withholds. The reason is in the first year there is much handling because it is thin and must be brought in and out; and there is an opposing view that the second year has more handling because it needs much feed; each has reason favoring him and he withholds from his fellow that the business continue until both periods end — Taz; he further wrote a question: one who receives iska from his fellow for a sum for a time, and after repayment time the recipient kept the money and engaged with it and does not want to give profit from what accrues after the time, saying the money was a deposit since he had no heter beyond that time and afterward it would be ribbis — Taz answered clearly the law is with the giver and he must give profit even from business after repayment time, and the initial heter continues until he notifies after the time that he no longer wants those funds in iska; and on the second question in the document where partial repayment was delayed and profit was claimed on the delayed portion — it appears the law is with him since the document explicitly states from today he accepts to engage with what is withheld even partially — see there:
baer-heitev/part-001.txt|24|א: He combines. Shach wrote otherwise it is forbidden due to ketzutza as above seif 6, for there is different since he cut in a known matter even if no profit; unlike here; and even if written in iska language it is forbidden; however Ritba wrote it appears if he leaves the document with a third party there is no concern and it is permitted:
baer-heitev/part-001.txt|24|ב: Loan. Even principal alone; Bach wrote although one cannot collect profit from him by force, if the recipient wishes to fulfill the verbal condition he stipulated he may accept from him since he gave it as iska; and if he stipulated verbally before witnesses we consider it as if the iska is explicit in the document and we extract from him by force; see Tur CM siman 18:
baer-heitev/part-001.txt|25|_: We judge. The vav of uvehefsed is a divider like or in loss; Prisha Hagahah wrote therefore give him wages as idle worker as above seif 2 letter 4, for here it is written in the document and appears more like ribbis; Beit Yosef wrote regarding another person if he preceded and seized iska we do not extract from him as asmakhta, but regarding a prominent person since it is obvious they did not stipulate forbidden matter we extract from him — see above s.k. 21:
baer-heitev/part-001.txt|27|_: A third. Taz wrote by way of example: if the loss is 24 gold coins, we say if this sum were profit the recipient would take 12; now he bears damage of 8 gold coins, and always proportionally — e.g. a quarter in wages to the recipient we say if there were damage he bears two-thirds of it, i.e. 4; and if he wrote he takes three parts in wages and the giver a quarter, damage falls on the recipient 12 — end quote:
baer-heitev/part-001.txt|31|_: He takes them. Mordekhai wrote even minor orphans take, and it deals when testimony was accepted in their father's lifetime, for then they are paid from them as in CM siman 108 — end quote Bach:
baer-heitev/part-001.txt|39|ב: Themselves. Lest what he bought for himself is not as good as the partnership and his fellow loses thereby. Where there is safek in the law or dispute among poskim whether ribbis ketzutza or asmakhta, it appears to be safek mamon lekula; the court should warn him he is doing forbidden matter and threaten him, and he should be stringent on himself; but if he pays no heed the court cannot extract since it is safek din; and apparently there is proof from what we say regarding priestly gifts as explained above siman 61 s.k. 23 and below regarding firstborn siman 305 s.k. 13 — Shach (ribbis issur is at start of loan even if borrower will not pay ribbis; Torat Emet siman 162; forbidden to lend with ribbis to give to poor or mitzvot; wealthy borrower and poor lender — forbidden; collateral loan with evasion sale — Tzitz Eliezer siman 20):
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|1|א: [Meaning etc. Tosafot in the name of Rabbenu Tam explain he sets a price on the flock and also sets the value of increase and accepts to give each year a fixed amount whether or not there is increase — we consider it as if it left the owner's domain and it is ribbis ketzutza; Beit Yosef wrote all agree on this for the law:]
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|2|ו: [And it must be etc. It implies iska too applies (where appreciation and depreciation and standing value apply) — i.e. R' Yitzchak's view in Tur and poskim; all the more when giving money for half profit, even the lenient agree as in Maharik shoresh 119 brought by Beit Yosef; on "there are lenient" Beit Yosef for R' Yitzchak's view — it seems the copier erred thinking the rabbi meant the recipient must accept all responsibility of the deposit half, not half of half; Beit Yosef clearly holds he must accept all responsibility of deposit half; what he wrote about accident responsibility equally means the whole business; the rabbi came to exclude Rivan's view that the giver accepting depreciation alone suffices — i.e. partial responsibility:]
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|4|_: And if they diminished the one engaging loses a third etc. This is Rambam's view, but most poskim disagree and hold the recipient takes two-thirds profit and bears half the loss — Beit Yosef brings them; wonder on the rabbi (and Taz) for not bringing them, and on Mechaber who generally follows Rif and Rosh when they agree with one view; Beit Yosef wrote Rif and Rosh hold they disagree on loss, and also Raavad, Ramban, Rashba, Ran, N.Y., Semag — and so appears the main Shas view; however all this in unspecified places, but where there is known custom we follow custom where no prohibition — HaTerumah in Raavad's name, brought by Beit Yosef:
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|5|א: [When he takes etc. Mordekhai chapter HaChovel wrote if Reuven lent Shimon money for a fixed time and after the time the lender told the borrower let it remain for half profit, the one engaging is liable for accidents as initially — Beit Yosef and Bach; so Maharshal chapter HaChovel siman 70; see above s.k. 38:]
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|8|_: One who lends etc. See above siman 172 and what is written there:
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|12|_: That lending with ribbis is. Although if he wished he could exempt himself at repayment etc. he is not believed, for a person does not make himself wicked — thus Semag's language; and it implies even for verbal loan he is not believed — Bach; see above siman 169 s.k. 37:
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|18|ב: [And they acquired from his hand etc. Regarding that it is not asmakhta as explained in CM siman 207:]
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|18|ג: [He is liable etc. Bach wrote this is specifically for Rabbenu Tam's view above siman 175 seif 6; it does not appear Mechaber's view, for he brought Rashbam's view first anonymously then Rabbenu Tam as "some say"; all agree since it is a penalty method it is permitted except forbidden due to ribbis evasion; here in selling merchandise since penalty method even ribbis evasion does not apply — as Ribash there:]
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|19|ב: [There is no ribbis. Since they did not give it as a loan and one cannot say close to profit and far from loss except where he stipulated to be far from loss and close to profit — Mordekhai there; and similarly Beit Yosef above siman 160 and Bach here in Rashba's responsum at length:]
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|34|_: I will not engage etc. Meaning he informed him of the loss and said I will not engage until you accept we split profit from today forward and profit will not be subordinate to principal — the power is in his hand; so explain Rashba's students — clear; Bach wrote these words are incomprehensible and it is a corruption; in my humble opinion as written:
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|38|_: Not clothing etc. Everything is included in produce except clothing and vessels — Rosh and later poskim; see above siman 217 s.k. 30 and siman 232 s.k. 8 for reason; but Rambam ch. 7 Sheluchin law 7 wrote he buys any kind he wishes and does not buy clothing or wood etc. — implying Rambam's reason is clothing and wood are not good merchandise, so where they are good merchandise he may buy; Kesef Mishneh wrote Rambam's reason is only produce mentioned is permitted, not things not called produce like clothing and wood; therefore Rambam's "and similarly" means similar not in produce category; now it fits what Rosh explicitly stated:
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|39|ב: [That he not sell together. Lest what he bought for himself is not as good as the partnership and his fellow loses — Beit Yosef and Acharonim; where safek in the law or dispute whether ribbis ketzutza or asmakhta — responsum R' Aharon Sasson siman 162 in Maharshal of Modena's name: we rule stringently as safek issur deoraita; he disagrees — safek mamon lekula; court should warn and he should be stringent; court cannot extract — safek din; proof from priestly gifts above siman 61 s.k. 23 and firstborn siman 305 s.k. 13 — Shach:]
turei-zahav/part-001.txt|3|_: As idle worker etc. Gemara teaches: idle worker — Abbaye said idle worker of that labor from which he is idle; Rashi explains if he first did heavy profitable labor and this is light, we estimate how much he would forgo from his wage for this lighter work; Tosafot challenged Rashi and explained idle worker means completely idle; Tosafot Bechorot 29b and Rosh similarly; Tosafot Bechorot explain like Kuntres since Gemara challenges there "he is not idle"; Beit Yosef explains we estimate how much a person would take to be completely idle from his work; Tur wrote we view a person who is idle with no work — how much he would take to engage in this business; even if he had work paying well and idles from it we do not say how much he would forgo but estimate an idle person; Maharshal in Chochmat Shlomo agreed with Tur's explanation and challenged Beit Yosef why ribbis differs from returning lost property; it appears no difficulty — Abbaye himself challenges and answers idle worker of that labor; Rambam and Tur both hold Sages were lenient in avak ribbis and we interpret according to context; Derishah challenged Tur on returning lost property; in my humble opinion both Beit Yosef and Tur are correct — Tosafot's language follows Beit Yosef; for completely idle person accepting iska we estimate what idle person would take, less than ordinary wage; even R' Meir who is lenient on wage between much and little only lenient for working person, not below idle person's rate — Beit Yosef aligns with Tur except Tur is stricter when he had work and idled completely; Beit Yosef's challenge on Tur's Gemara question is answered — we estimate idle person even for heavy labor; Tosafot's challenge on Rashi cannot be answered that way since Rashi has no leniency at all — Mishnah follows R' Shimon requiring full compensation for loss:
turei-zahav/part-001.txt|5|_: Since he has another business. It implies if he has no other business it is forbidden since he does not reach the measure Chazal said — two-thirds in wages and half in loss; wonder, for Rambam himself wrote ch. 6 Sheluchin: if the engaging one's profit exceeds his loss, even less than a sixth it is permitted even without another business; Beit Yosef answered here deals when they did not stipulate initially but at accounting said if profit, third or tenth as wages; Tur's "or similarly gives a dinar all days of partnership" is hard — implies one who did not stipulate initially, but Rif and Rosh wrote the enactment two-thirds and half applies when stipulating initially; Maharshal explains Tur's dinar is Shmuel's "he cuts a dinar" before giving iska; Tur does not usually disagree with Rashi and Tosafot; Beit Yosef explained "or similarly" when he has another business; I explain for law when iska already done and he claims wages at division, or accepted before engaging — dinar suffices before accepting; but not for first two division cases after acceptance; Tur's view: not specifically two-thirds/half but any case recipient profits more in gain than loses in loss, as Beit Yosef explained R' Yitzchak and Rosh — "or similarly gives dinar" means takes more profit share even tenth if only dinar total wages, as long as he accepts more in profit than in loss:
turei-zahav/part-001.txt|9|_: As paid custodian. Although he gives wages only for engaging in his portion, the benefit of finding money to do business with is considered as taking wages for guarding them. It appears if the iska is such that by engaging in the deposit portion he profits in his loan portion too — e.g. buying better merchandise together or shared transport costs — he need not give wages as this is better than two-thirds enactment; we find similar in Yerushalmi and Ketubot 92; Gemara Bava Metzia 104 regarding iska half loan — recipient cannot drink beer from loan portion; if such iska existed recipient would harm giver's deposit profit; partners case confirms Gemara does not deal with such iska; but where there is such benefit he need not give wages — in my humble opinion:
turei-zahav/part-001.txt|12|_: And he cut in a known matter etc. Tur likewise in R' Yeshaya's name — reason it appears as loan with ribbis and leads to full ribbis; wonder where R' Yeshaya learned to decree what Talmud did not; perhaps he learned from leaseholders siman 164 forbidden to re-lease for fixed sum — Rambam, Ramban, Rashba hold ribbis evasion; opposite case — giver buying uncertainty from recipient for fixed sum is permitted; giving sum for business with fixed sum if profit and nothing if loss is daily practice in communities with iska documents — no concern if loss responsibility is on both:
turei-zahav/part-001.txt|26|_: If one gives merchandise as iska. Beit Yosef here in Rosh klal 88: if iska began forbidden — sold wheat below market to get money and did not give idle wages — he takes no profit; Beit Yosef explained if given unspecified he takes wages per above seif 3-4, but this forbidden case even idle wages would partially cancel issur and he would take half profit at market rate when money given; since only forbidden stipulation he takes no profit:
turei-zahav/part-001.txt|31|_: For a thin animal 30 days etc. Question: recipient took iska for a sum for a time; after repayment time he kept money and engaged, refusing profit after time saying money became deposit without heter — ribbis if he pays. Second question in document: partial delay with explicit stipulation from today to engage with withheld sum — first: law with giver, must give profit after time, initial heter continues until notification; proof from Bava Metzia 69 — after 30/50 days recipient takes half his and half of half of fellow's increase; Beit Yosef in Rashba's students' name same for money iska; Rambam ch. 8 — half of fellow's only if placed offspring and stipulated before three; Tur: must notify fellow; Beit Yosef they do not disagree. At minimum recipient takes from profit after fixed time; not merely deposit after time while business remains in hand from outset unless notified then new business; proof Rava — one who accepted iska and lost, toiled and filled without notifying cannot say therefore I toiled; shame to withhold after time; surely continued for business benefit. Second question: if profit becomes principal after time — Yerushalmi/N.Y. two partners, profit to principal, custom not to divide until end; here explicit document stipulation overrides Yerushalmi custom:
turei-zahav/part-001.txt|32|_: From then on he takes half the increase etc. Gemara: from then on he takes half his and half of half of fellow's — Rashi: recipient takes full half for his portion and half of increase in fellow's half as wages like mother's animal half wages; Rav Menasya took half his and half of half — Abbaye: who divided for you; further, place where custom to raise — we learn no increase without seven; Beit Yosef: two explanations in Rashba's students — Rashi: until proper division he takes nothing from fellow's increase; Tosafot: even without division he takes half of fellow's increase after time; Rambam implies like Rashi — must appraise before three or they divide equally; Tur: if divided without notification still partners each takes half; Prisha challenged Tur; I explain Tur like Tosafot — if he divided and revealed he does not want to guard without division, division void and no share in fellow's portion; unlike undivided unspecified iska where Tosafot applies; when he thought division valid until Abbaye revealed, still took from fellow's per Tosafot; Bach and Prisha differ; I side with Bach and Shulchan Aruch follows Tur — recipient has no rights in giver's portion until proper division before three or notification:
turei-zahav/part-001.txt|35|_: Two-thirds of the part he was profiting. It appears Rambam, mara de'atra, per Gemara: if half in wages, two-thirds in loss; if half in loss, two-thirds in wages; Rashi: first clause on giver, second on recipient; Rambam all on recipient — if stipulated half in wages and not in loss, he bears two-thirds of loss calculated as if that loss were profit share; example loss 24 — if profit he would take 12, now bears 8; proportionally e.g. quarter wages — if damage, recipient bears two-thirds (4); if three parts wages and giver quarter, damage on recipient 12. If half loss stipulated without profit clause — two-thirds in wages: if profit 24 he takes 16; not from sum as if loss like first clause. If quarter loss on recipient without profit clause — two-thirds in wages: calculate as if giver would bear three-quarters of hypothetical loss 18, recipient takes two-thirds of 18 = 12. Main girsa not "takes a third" — Ramban follows recipient's share always; Rambam rejects — recipient should not take only 8 and giver 16. General rule: for loss follow loan portion — recipient pays only third of loss on his share; for profit follow deposit portion — recipient takes extra third from deposit share beyond his half; Kesef Mishneh ch. 6 explains; if three parts loss stipulated, no two-thirds in wages — profit per above from loss share plus fellow's third:
nekudot-hakesef/part-001.txt|1|_: (Siman 177 Taz s.k. 3) Already in most of his words Derishah, Bach in last pamphlet, Maharash Iddels, Maharam Lublin in their chiddushim and other Acharonim preceded him; but some of his words and some Acharonim's are not straight in my humble opinion as I will explain. Bach's long passage "leave the rest to sages of the generation" — unclear to me; sages' words seem correct — what if there is much toil, is he not paid according to labor weight? If you say Tur and Maharshal hold so — not true; truth is Beit Yosef's understanding; we too say all sages challenged Maharshal on Beit Yosef for not going deep — otherwise challenge in Eizehu Neshech "he is not idle" since Rosh explained Sages lenient in avak ribbis; why didn't Tosafot explain returning lost property similarly; how does their challenge depend on taking wages for returning lost property? They also challenged from Tosafot Bechorot per Beit Yosef — all explained at length in Torat Chaim, Maharsha, Maharam Lublin, Maadanei Melech ch. Eizehu Neshech, Derishah, Bach; they say Maharshal erred. I will explain Maharshal's intent and defend him from all challenges. Maharshal surely knew Sages lenient here in avak ribbis; but this enactment of idle worker wages is so he not appear to toil on deposit portion free — how could Sages enact he not pay for current labor, still appears as ribbis; if because Sages lenient in avak ribbis they should enact opposite — not take wages for idling from first labor; therefore Maharshal: Tosafot's answer "completely idle" only excludes Rashi who pays for both labors — one payment for one labor and first as completely idle; Sages enacted per context — in ribbis pay for second labor so not appear to toil on second free; in lost property paying for second appears as taking wages for returning lost property so not pay for second, pay for idling from first. Maharshal's challenge stands: even per Beit Yosef, challenge in ribbis "not idle from current labor" still appears as ribbis — leniency in avak ribbis only for not paying idling from first; obviously still appears as ribbis if not paying for current labor; Tosafot cannot explain lost property like ribbis since Gemara challenges "not idle" meaning he may take wages for toiling on lost property; if permitted to take wages for returning lost property, why deduct anything — like optional labor not mitzvah; cannot say Abbaye answers completely idle deducting for first labor since permitted to take wages, why deduct; since not deducting for second, all the more not for first — in lost property more reasonable not pay for second; certainly answers like Kuntres; Tosafot Bechorot deduct for second labor since generally forbidden to take wages for legal work which is second labor — no question from all sages' challenges — examine well. Derishah end wondered on Beit Yosef — Tur follows R' Chananel, Ramban, Rashba — not well aimed; Tur's explanation unrelated to them — they pay nothing for second labor; then Gemara question fits only paying for first at reduced rate unlike Tur; R' Chananel in Tosafot ch. Ad Kamah is same, copied from ch. Elu Metziot and ch. E.N. — one intent; see Ramban Milchamot ch. E.N.
